applicableAreas: Eastern property boundary; wood fence location
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a wood fence running along the eastern property boundary, labeled as adjacent to a 5' Electric Easement (Vol. 69, Pg. 14). This fence is located within or immediately adjacent to an AE easement that requires AE access for installation, maintenance, and repair of electric facilities. The site plan notes and general notes on Sheet 3 do not reference or indicate that a license agreement has been obtained from AE Property Agents and AE Design for this fence installation within the easement. Vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirmed fence placement directly along the easement boundary.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10 requires license agreements for landscaping, trees, encroachments, or construction activities within AE easements. These agreements must be reviewed and approved by both AE Property Agents and AE Design prior to site plan approval. The wood fence appears to constitute an encroachment or improvement within the AE easement. No license agreement is documented on the site plan, and the absence of this required coordination represents non-compliance with the license agreement requirement.
findings.comment: Wood fence is located within or immediately adjacent to AE easement on the eastern property boundary, but no license agreement with AE Property Agents and AE Design is documented on the site plan. License agreement approval must be obtained and submitted for this fence installation within the AE easement.

applicableAreas: Eastern property boundary; wood fence adjacent to AE easement
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts a wood fence running along the eastern property boundary, immediately adjacent to or within the 5' Electric Easement. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) references the same fence. Block 9 on Sheet 9 contains only a brief 'Fence Note' that addresses post hole installation in Critical Root Zones (CRZs), requiring hand-digging and mulch application. No construction details, material specifications, profile views, section drawings, or structural details are provided for the wood fence on any sheet reviewed (Sheets 9, 22-39).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires construction details of fences to be provided when fencing is proposed in proximity to AE facilities. The fence's location adjacent to an AE easement qualifies as proximity to AE facilities. The site plan provides only a note about CRZ post hole installation but no fence construction details. The absence of detailed fence construction documentation prevents AE Design review and preliminary approval as required by the code.
findings.comment: Fencing is proposed adjacent to AE electric easement on the eastern property boundary, but construction details and specifications are not provided. Provide detailed fence construction drawings including profiles, sections, materials, post spacing, and foundation details for AE Design review and approval.

applicableAreas: Eastern property boundary; wood fence and AE easement
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) both show a wood fence on the eastern property boundary adjacent to the 5' Electric Easement. Review of construction detail sheets (Sheets 22-28) shows only standard details for curbs, sidewalks, water infrastructure, wastewater, and storm drain features; no fence profile plan or detail drawings are provided. Sheet 38-39 contain retaining wall details but not fence details. No profile plan view or section views of the fence and adjacent AE easement/facilities are present.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires profile plans and detail drawings of fences and existing utility facilities when fence installation may affect or be near existing AE utilities. These drawings must be submitted for AE Design review and preliminary approval. The site plan is missing the required profile plan (showing fence alignment relative to the easement in plan view with elevation references) and detail sections (showing fence dimensions, materials, post placement, and relationship to the underlying easement).
findings.comment: No profile plan or detail drawings are provided for the wood fence near the AE electric easement on the eastern boundary. Submit profile plan view showing fence alignment and easement boundary relationship, and provide section details showing fence construction, post spacing, materials, and clearances to AE facilities for AE Design review and preliminary approval.

applicableAreas: Transformers 1, 2, and 3 locations; building meter locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows three electrical transformer pads and six meter locations (on building exteriors). Vision analysis measured separation distances between transformer pads and associated meter banks: Transformer 1 to meters range 30-50 feet; Transformer 2 to meters range 10-150 feet; Transformer 3 to meters range 60-150 feet. The transformers are located in standalone pads in easements/common areas, while meters are mounted on building walls. These two types of equipment are not grouped together in common locations. Some meter/transformer pairs may have line-of-sight obstructions created by building corners.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1(I) requires meters and disconnects to be grouped together in a common location, with maximum 20-foot separation, and within line of sight of each other. The separation distances measured on the electrical plan exceed the 20-foot maximum threshold for multiple transformer/meter combinations. Additionally, transformers and meters are not grouped in a common location but are dispersed across the site (transformers in separate pads; meters on individual building exteriors). The requirement for line of sight is potentially not met where building structures create obstructions between transformer pads and associated meters.
findings.comment: Meters and transformers are not grouped in a common location and are separated by more than 20 feet in multiple instances, exceeding the maximum separation allowed. Some meter/transformer pairs may lack adequate line of sight. Reconfigure electrical infrastructure to group meters and disconnects in common locations within 20 feet of each transformer, with clear line of sight maintained between all paired equipment.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) depicts three transformer pads. Vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) confirms that Transformer 3 (located between Buildings 6 and 7 on the east side of the site) is positioned within a paved area with surface parking spaces to the northwest and the main concrete drive aisle immediately adjacent. The transformer is clearly within 4 feet of parking and traffic circulation areas. Sheet 21 shows the transformer pad symbol but contains no indication of bollards, protective posts, or any barrier/protection device at this location. No detail sheet (Sheets 22-39) provides bollard details for this transformer location.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal posts (bollards) per AE Design equipment pad details for pad-mounted equipment located within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. Transformer 3 is clearly within 4 feet of surface parking spaces and a paved drive aisle. The absence of bollards shown on the electrical plan or detail sheets indicates this requirement has not been addressed. Bollards are required to protect the transformer pad from vehicular impact and to maintain safe clearance from traffic.
findings.comment: Transformer 3 is located within 4 feet of surface parking and drive aisle but no bollards are shown. Provide 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollard posts per AE Design equipment pad details, positioned to protect the transformer pad from vehicular impact and maintain required clearances.

applicableAreas: Detention pond and northeast site area; electrical infrastructure
findings.observation: Sheet 15 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan & Calculations) shows the pond located in the northeast corner of the site. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) depicts pull boxes and underground electrical lines routing through the eastern portion of the site near the pond area. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows drainage easements in the NE area. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 indicated that pull boxes are present in the vicinity of drainage easements on the eastern side but did not identify transformer pads or major electrical equipment in the immediate proximity of the pond basin itself. However, the electrical infrastructure routing in the northeast area requires verification of specific clearances and separation distances from the pond, its retaining walls, and the pond perimeter fence shown on Sheet 9.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.0 requires electric facilities conflicts with proposed ponds and water features to be resolved per AE criteria. While vision analysis suggests transformer pads are not in immediate pond proximity, the presence of pull boxes, underground lines, and drainage easements in the same general area requires explicit verification that all electrical infrastructure meets required clearances from the pond structure, perimeter fence, and water surface. The distance between the electrical pull boxes and the pond edge cannot be definitively measured from the current plan sheets without specific dimensions or clearance callouts.
findings.comment: Electrical infrastructure (pull boxes and underground lines) is shown in the northeast area near the detention pond. Provide specific clearance distances and verify that all electrical equipment, lines, and pull boxes maintain required separation from the pond structure, retaining walls, perimeter fence, and water surface per AE design criteria.
